pr_title: Fix bug in check_config when an integration is removed by its own validator
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
As found out in #96061, the integrations `tradfri` and `webostv` were blocking restart without a clear error message. When checking the code, both had `cv.removed(DOMAIN, raise_if_present=False)`, meaning that the field should be removed, but it isn't a big deal so we don't raise an exception. 

Except, after `config = config_schema(config)`, the `tradfri` key is gone from the config because of the `cv.removed`. When accessed in the next line, it threw a KeyError.

This also solves the verify configuration feature in Developer tools from returning a 500 (and the frontend just says that it's still loading).

comments:
Solved, but maybe for future reference interesting

I had these two entries in my configuration.yaml

```
webostv:
    host: 192.168.1.211
    turn_on_action:
     service: wake_on_lan.send_magic_packet
     data:
       mac: 55-44-33-22-3a-86
       broadcast_address: 192.168.1.255
```
and
```
tradfri:
  allow_tradfri_groups: true
```

removing them solved the problem.
They were useless anyway, but imho I dont think they should have prevented the system from restarting...

This is because of the migration to configuration via the UI. When removing the yaml configuration we also add code to import the current configuration and create an issue to show the user that they should remove the yaml (as it's generally a good practice to have your configuration in sync to be able to deliver what you expect, for example, if your tv changed IP for some reason and you edit it here, it wouldn't have changed in the configuration, which makes it confusing).

It could have been that you maybe didn't see those issues, maybe because of skipping a release or some other reason. Since 2023.7.0, the deprecation period is now 6 months. So if you use an integration that is moving to the UI, your stuff will be imported and you will be notified that you need to remove yaml configuration. And since it's now 6 months instead of 3, you're less likely to miss it when skipping a release.

I do have to say that the error could be a lot better. I saw your issue first and was like, this is strange. And now you posted the solution I am like, this makes sense now. So I'll have a look at how that works.

Thanks @joostlek  for your explanantion!  I did however always remove obsolete yaml configuration whenever an upgrade mentioned it. The two causing the problem where never listed as obsolete and I think that has everything to do with the fact that they seem more or less undocumented ( and from a long time ago :) 

Still, I dont understand why it did block restarting?    I did notice however that the 'configuration verify' stopped working.

I just saw a bug. Both `webostv` and `tradfri` have their config schemas set to `cv.removed(DOMAIN, raise_if_present=False)`, meaning this field shouldn't be there, but don't raise an exception if it is. So it did not raise that specific exception, but it did raise another one which has the unclear error message.

This is also the cause of the not working verify configuration

```suggestion
                # Don't fail if the validator removed the domain from the config
                if domain in config:
```

I think we should show the config is invalid here and not just silent let it pass. This will not effect startop but urge users to cleanup the removed config.

```suggestion
                if domain in config:
                    result[domain] = config[domain]
                else:
                    result.add_error(f"Config found for {domain} in configration.yaml. "
                                      "YAML support for this domain has been removed. "
                                      "Please remove if from your configration.yaml.")
```

test would need to change. E.g.

```python
async def test_removed_yaml_support(hass: HomeAssistant) -> None:
    """Test config validation check with removed CONFIG_SCHEMA without raise if present."""
    mock_integration(
        hass,
        MockModule(domain="bla", config_schema=cv.removed("bla", raise_if_present=False)),
        False
    )
    files = {YAML_CONFIG_FILE: BASE_CONFIG + "bla:\n  platform: demo"}
    with patch("os.path.isfile", return_value=True), patch_yaml_files(files):
        res = await async_check_ha_config_file(hass)
        log_ha_config(res)

        assert res.keys() == {"homeassistant"}
        assert res.error_str.startswith("Invalid config for [bla]: Config found for bla in configration.yaml.")
```

This message is still being shown with raise_if_present=False. I'll send a log tomorrow. If we really want to throw a vol.Invalid and treat it like an invalid config, raise_if_missing=True would be enough.

It will not raise when starting up HA, only when you try to restart, so it should not break startup, But in fact it is an invalid config, that is why it should fail. An alternative be registering an issue in the issue registry.
